page.title: Best Platform for Virtual Events Buyer Guide
page.description: Compare formats, cost models, engagement tools, production needs and follow‑up analytics to choose the right virtual event platform.
page.h1: What is the best platform for virtual events?
page.definition: A virtual event platform is software that hosts live or recorded online gatherings, handling registration, streaming, interaction, recording and post‑event data for audiences of any size. It also integrates with marketing automation, CRM and analytics tools to turn attendees into leads.
page.quick_answer: List your format, audience size and must‑have interaction features first, then match them to a cost model and production plan before signing a contract. Run a full rehearsal on the chosen platform two to five days before go‑live.

sections.h2: What event format and audience size do you need?

blocks.p: The format and expected attendance dictate which platform tier can support you. A single‑track webinar for a few hundred people needs far less capacity than a multi‑track conference with thousands of concurrent viewers.

blocks.p: Interaction tools determine whether attendees stay or drop off. Prioritise features that match your content style and audience expectations.

sections.h2: How will you handle production and rehearsal?

blocks.p: Production is separate from the platform and must be planned early. A dedicated crew owns the run of show, speaker prep and backup stream.

sections.h2: What follow‑up and analytics do you require?

blocks.p: Post‑event data turns attendance into pipeline. Choose a platform that feeds the metrics your sales and marketing teams rely on.

ul: Automated replay delivery within twenty‑four to forty‑eight hours

faq.q: How far in advance should I book a platform for a multi‑track conference?
faq.a: Reserve the platform and lock venue AV at least six to eight weeks before the event, then finalize the agenda and speaker rehearsals. This timeline also allows time for integration with registration and marketing automation tools. A buffer of one week handles unexpected technical reviews.

faq.q: What is the difference between a platform licence and a production crew?
faq.a: The platform licence provides the streaming software and attendee management, while the production crew supplies cameras, encoders, a run of show and a backup stream. You purchase both separately; the platform is a subscription, production is a service engagement. West Peek Productions can provide the crew on the platform you already use.

faq.q: Which engagement tools drive the highest attendee retention?
faq.a: Live Q&A with a dedicated moderator, real‑time polls and breakout rooms consistently keep viewers past the halfway mark. Adding gamified leaderboards and threaded chat further extends average watch time by a noticeable margin. Plan at least one interactive element every ten minutes of content.

faq.q: When should the replay be sent to attendees?
faq.a: Deliver the edited recording within twenty‑four to forty‑eight hours after the live session while the experience is still fresh. Include timestamped chapters, a downloadable slide deck and a short feedback form to capture immediate sentiment. Automate the email through your marketing platform so no manual step is missed.
